title: Volume 2 Chapter 1: To You Whom I Can Reach with My Hand, But Whose Voice Cannot Reach Me 3
content: "Since there are two Longdaggers, Shin is fine."
After saying that, I realized something.
"By the way, what's your name?"
"Barel. I told you the other day, remember?"
Barel answered, exasperated.
"I heard that from the Longdagger with the beard."
Barel snorted at my sarcasm.
The speed at which we became informal was typical of adventurers, and it made me a bit happy.
In a world governed by self-responsibility and meritocracy, this straightforwardness was refreshing.
It was completely different from the noble society where you had to invite someone over for tea, engage in some minor scheming, and share common interests before you could even be considered friends.
It was truly comfortable.
As I nodded, thinking that this was the life of an adventurer, Barel shot me a look that was anything but polite.
It was a look of disbelief.
"By the way, can't you do something about that sister of yours?"
At Barel's words, I turned my gaze to the presence I had been avoiding all this time.
She was busy treating the injured.
Shara was going around casting Healing Magic on anyone who needed it.
At first, she was welcomed, but after one of the recipients screamed in agony from the pain of her healing, it became clear that she was now feared.
Healing Magic is known for taking time to learn, but even more so for the significant difference in effectiveness depending on the user's skill.
Specifically, if someone casts Healing Magic poorly, it hurts.
A lot.
When Shara healed someone who was already struggling to move due to injury, she would then chase after those who could still move, trying to heal them next.
Terrifyingly, the screams elicited while being bitten by a monster were less painful than those cried out during her healing.
How could she belong to the Healing Faction of the Church, which believes in saving the weak with such a skill level?
I averted my gaze from Barel, who looked like he wanted to say,
"Do something about it.
" Please don't let him think I'm associated with her.
I resolutely ignored Barel's request.
"Turning your eyes away won't change reality, Hairless Longdagger."
Stop it, you fool. The harsh reality is that I'm just the husband in this farce.
If I were to be confronted with that sister on top of it, I might just cry.
"That said..."
Determined to avoid making eye contact with Shara, I focused intently on Barel.
"Why are those guys digging in a place like this?"
When I turned around, Shara came into view.
I pointed with my thumb at the group desperately digging into the ground and asked Barel.
The place where they should be digging was a bit further ahead.
"Huh?"
Barel froze, making an interesting face.

Erika Solnzali, the first daughter of a prestigious marquis family in the Faltarl Kingdom, a genius of sword and magic, and falsely accused of plotting to assassinate the Light Priestess, was exiled from her homeland──.
It was incredibly fun.
No, it was really, really fun.
I had thought the same when I first fought monsters in the plains with Shin; how exhilarating it was to fight freely in such a wide space.
Erika tightened her lips, which were about to curve into a smile.
No, no, that's not right. Smiling here would be unbecoming of a lady.
Shin had stepped back to give me room to move freely, watching over the whole situation.
It felt wrong to enjoy fighting in front of him like this.
Moreover, even though it was a farce, I was his wife. Shin's wife.
To gleefully wreak havoc after being given permission by my husband seems rather inappropriate for a lady, doesn't it?
...No, but isn't it already inappropriate for a lady to be wreaking havoc in the first place?
As I sliced through the monsters I had only learned about in class, burned them with magic, and sent them flying, I pondered.
It wasn't about the feeling of impact, so my mind was free.
When I felt that freedom, my thoughts began to scatter.
I accidentally recalled Shin's name from earlier and miscalculated my strength.
What was the name of that monster that flew so high into the air?
I tried to remember the name I had learned in class, but for some reason, I kept picturing Shin praising me excessively.
I miscalculated my strength again.
Several monsters exploded without leaving a single magic stone behind.
Just the other day, I had struggled with money.
Erika reflected on this.
No, is this really my fault?
[img]../image/i-049.jpg
I understood Shin's intentions, but I couldn't help but think that praising someone so openly in public was a bit much.
I wasn't used to such direct compliments, and just recalling them made me blush.
As I carefully sliced through three charging Shield Boars, I pondered seriously whether ordinary couples praised each other like that.
I felt like I couldn't do that.
But then again, I was the one who dragged Shin into this.
Shin called me his wife for the sake of the farce and praised me in front of others.
If I hesitated just because it embarrassed me, wouldn't that be a betrayal?
But to praise him so directly... how would I even do that?
I could only think of noble ways to express it, and as I sliced off a monster's head, I pondered what to do.
Just then, I heard an adventurer who had been talking to Shin shout.
"The designated subjugation target should be right here! What's going on, Longdagger?!"
I’m also a Longdagger, you know.
I thought to myself, tilting my head in confusion.
The designated subjugation target should have been here.
Barel's words left me greatly bewildered.
"Even if you say that, we defeated it a bit further ahead, you know?"
I pointed to the spot where a hill once stood.
What I had thought was a hill, the massive Forest Dragon, was no longer there, leaving just a plain.
But we had indeed fought the dragon over there.
In the Demon Realm, plants are said to be a type of magic, so the ground that Erika had blown away with her magic was now covered in grass.
Not enough time had passed for it to be unrecognizable.
Don't be ridiculous, the opponent is the master of the designated subjugation target, right?
There’s no way it would have moved that far away while we were fighting.
Well, that's true.
I didn't understand the reasoning, but a master is typically a creature that clings to a specific location.
When I was in the Faltarl Kingdom, I sometimes accompanied my master on hunts for masters, but generally, they wouldn't stray far unless they were blown away by my master.
Even when they were pummeled by my master, they didn't try to escape, which showed their tenacity.
But if that were the case, the Adventurer Guild wouldn't just leave a master unattended.
Designated subjugation targets referred to as masters are usually dangerous monsters.
If they were moving around and causing damage, the guild would go all out to subdue them.
"Hey, Longdagger."
Barel said, beads of sweat forming on his stern face.
"I have a bad feeling about this. I definitely have a bad feeling."
The adventurers, who had gained some confidence, were now beating down the remaining monsters.
Surround them! Surround them! Let's bag them!
Hearing those small-time voices felt like a distant event, and I almost tried to make a lighthearted joke, but I held my tongue.
It wasn't that I thought my own words sounded small-time.
It was just that I remembered a similar situation that had happened recently.
What had appeared back then was a massive Forest Dragon that looked like a castle.
No way, right? There couldn't possibly be another Forest Dragon hiding underground.
When I calmed down and thought about it, it really was impossible.
It was just a coincidence that there were similar monsters near the designated subjugation target, and that there were two of them.
Furthermore, there was no way the original designated target was hiding.
"Shin, is something wrong?"
As I conveyed my disbelief to Barel with just my expression, Erika called out to me.
Despite having just been slicing through monsters with ease, Erika was not even covered in dirt or blood.
If it were me, I would be a bloody mess.
As expected of Erika.
Seeing her elegantly flick the blood off her sword with a cool sound made me feel pity for the academy students who would never see this side of her.
Even her best friend, the Light Priestess, had probably never seen it.
In other words, I was the only one. I was the only person from Faltarl who knew Erika could fight so freely.
That sense of being the only one who knew made me want to grin, but I forced myself to keep a straight face.
That said, I had to respond to Erika's voice.
Well, this girl is thinking something foolish.
I was about to say something lighthearted, like,
"Hey, dear, can I tell you something?
" when Erika was suddenly sent flying into the air.
As I watched Erika soar high into the sky, Barel gasped in surprise, and I sighed at the beauty of her magical technique and the grace of her body control.
Rather than being blown away, Erika had leaped into the air herself, gracefully adjusting her posture mid-flight before landing next to me, who had taken a step back.
"I was caught off guard."
She muttered with a hint of dissatisfaction, brushing her disheveled red hair aside, making my heart race.
The golden magical power emanating from her gaze was directed straight at the creature that had emerged from the ground, and she frowned in displeasure.
Perhaps she was upset about being caught off guard?
Now that I think about it, I don't know anyone else who can see magical power besides me, so I was the only one who knew about her golden magical power.
I shouldn't smile.
"Another dragon appeared! Why!? Three dragons in two days!?"
"Damn it! I knew it!"
Shara and Barel shouted from behind.
As I watched the creature shaking off dirt and debris, I wondered what to do.
"What happens in this case, I wonder?"
"What do you mean?"
Erika tilted her head at my spontaneous question.
"I think this is a mistake on the Adventurer Guild's part."
I pointed at the Forest Dragon that had emerged from the ground.
As expected of the Demon Realm.
To have three masters in the same place is something I've never heard of.
Watching the adventurers flounder in confusion at the suddenly appeared dragon, Erika said as if it were the most natural thing in the world.
"Can't we just defeat it?"
That's true. I calmed myself, almost convinced.
"Well, I'm worried about whether we can be recognized as having defeated the master."
Ah, I see, Erika murmured softly.
However, she frowned, clearly dissatisfied, and I almost felt like going to the guild to protest immediately.
Who was it that made Erika look like that?
"Isn't the one we defeated much smaller than this one?"
"That one is still larger than usual, Erika."
As I corrected Erika's mistake, I realized I understood her dissatisfaction.
Well, certainly, if they said that the massive one that looked like a castle wasn't a master, I would want to say,
"Wait a minute.
"Hey! Longdagger! Didn't you defeat it!?"
I thought that if we defeated this one, the guild would recognize us, but then Barel grabbed my shoulder from behind.
"We did defeat it, the one that was as big as a castle."
At my response, Barel exclaimed, "Huh!?" in disbelief, shouting that he didn't understand.
I understood how he felt. I didn't understand either.
"Well, there's no helping it. Let's defeat it again."
"Are we going to use the same method?"
I looked at Shara at Erika's words.
She was staring blankly at the dragon with a face that looked like she might cry.
For her, this was the unexpected third dragon. It was only natural for her to look like that.
"If we make Shara do the same thing now, it seems like the adventurers would get blown away too, so let's not."
At my words, Erika nodded seriously, understanding. Erika was practical in these matters.
"What are you all talking about?"
Barel asked, his voice filled with doubt about our sanity, but I ignored him.

The Forest Dragon, which had emerged from underground and was now looking around as if deciding who to start a bloodbath with—by the way, it was about the size of three carriages—had a change in atmosphere.
Oh? It made eye contact with me.
I drew my sword and said,
"I'm going to beat it up with my wife."
I implied that I was telling the other adventurers not to get too close──.
"Beating it up sounds rather crude, Shin. But, well, let's say we’ll slice it up?"
Erika's attempt to use unfamiliar words was adorable.
The dragon roared.
"So, let's add another Forest Dragon magic stone to the mix."
Fugah!
An adventurer guild staff member named Rana was brought before me, held tightly from behind by her colleagues, and she shouted something.
By the way, I was definitely not at fault this time.
I had gone to the counter where there were staff members who weren't Rana.
If they came from the other side, it shouldn't be my responsibility.
Rana, who was thrown in front of me like a
"poof!
" was glaring at me with teary eyes.
Hey, stop it, it looks like I made her cry.
Are you asking for an explanation?
I think it's only natural to offer a bit of mercy to someone about to be executed, but are you asking for an explanation?
"It’s the guild's fault."
At my explanation, Rana's eyebrows shot up at a sharp angle.
The guild staff who dealt with my master, "Kind Barbara," in Faltarl often made that same face.
In other words, it was the face of someone swallowing a spiked iron ball while furrowing their brow.
"There was a third Forest Dragon in the same place."
Guuuh! Rana made a sound as if she had swallowed the spiked ball.
"That is indeed a flaw on the guild's part."
After swallowing her words, Rana acknowledged it.
As she recognized, this was undoubtedly a flaw on the guild's side.
The designated subjugation targets are specified by the guild, and because of that, the responsibility for that information lies with the guild.
The previous request only mentioned one Forest Dragon, but in reality, there was another one, a massive castle-like Forest Dragon.
Even that would be a significant problem for the guild.
When the guild sets designated subjugation targets, they usually dispatch a specialized party to confirm them.
This time, they had made a significant mistake, which would lead to a rather serious situation for the guild.
If they let adventurers die due to a faulty request, it would become a matter of the guild's credibility.
In the previous case, we had managed to brush it off as a coincidence of encountering similar monsters.
However, with a third one, it would be hard to sweep it under the rug.
Not for me, but for the guild.
"We should... we should probably thank you, huh?"
Rana's face seemed to say she wanted to go get the guild master right now and leave the rest to them.
"Well, as long as you buy the Forest Dragon magic stones without delay, I don't mind."
In an instant, Rana's face brightened with a "Seriously?!"
In reality──, it's an obvious fact, but whether it's a designated subjugation request or a regular request, adventurers don't just hunt the targeted monster and call it a day.
It's normal for adventurers to defeat other monsters to fulfill a request.
Even for designated subjugation requests, no adventurer believes the content blindly.
Those who are that naive will soon find themselves dead.
Survival is key for us adventurers. If we're going to clash with the unreasonable, we learn to question everything.
The only exception is Erika. She is the truth itself.
While we appreciate Longdagger-sama's generosity, the guild will make further efforts to provide more accurate information to all adventurers...
And the guild staff who accompany such adventurers also become suspicious.
Even if you look at me with those eyes, nothing will come out, you know?
"We won't be raising your adventurer rank to a special 7 or anything?"
"I don't want that."
This guy has really lost all sense of restraint.
Just a little while ago, he had a timid, small animal-like demeanor, but now there's not a trace of it.
"As long as you properly buy the Forest Dragon magic stones, that's all I need."
As I signed the document handed to me, I placed the magic stone on the counter.
Since it was a magic stone from a Forest Dragon the size of three carriages, it should be larger than usual.
However, having just seen the massive castle-like one and the house-sized one, it felt small.
"Ugh, this looks so small."
It seemed she felt the same way, as she muttered in dismay while taking the magic stone in her hands and examining it.
"When you put it up for auction consecutively, the price tends to drop. What will you do?"
I'll pass on the auction for ours.
Just the guild's purchase is fine.
We just happened to encounter and defeat it by chance.
Just handle it well on your end as a nuisance fee.
Since I wasn't in need of money right now, I could afford to wait.
Conversely, since I wasn't in need of money, there was no reason to wait.
The guild's purchase price is lower than what I could get at auction, but right now, that didn't matter.
Besides──, I had another magic stone.
As I received the bag with the payment for the magic stone from Rana, I turned around and called out.
So, you guys are lucky.
It seems a veteran guild staff member who is experienced in buying Forest Dragon magic stones will properly buy them.
Even if you put them up for auction, they are quite experienced.
"Thanks for that, Longdagger," Barel said, while Rana shouted, "You tricked us, Longdagger!"
Tricked? That's such a bad way to put it.
I just introduced a guild staff member who was skilled at handling large magic stones.
"Let me go! I can't take any more overtime! Please let me go!"
With Rana shouting as she was held tightly by other guild staff on the other side of the counter, I left the guild.
At the entrance of the guild, Erika and Shara were waiting for me.
The looks of disbelief on their faces were probably just my misunderstanding.
